questions.question: Describe the golden triangle and explain how each element depends on the other two.

points.text: The golden triangle is the interdependent relationship between sport, media and sponsorship. Sport provides content and audiences for the media. Media provides exposure and a platform for sponsors to display their brands. Sponsors provide the funding that sport needs to operate and develop. questions.question: How has social media changed the relationship between sport and sponsorship?

questions.question: Explain why commercialisation can be both beneficial and harmful for spectators.

points.text: Beneficial for spectators: More live sport is available through TV, streaming and social media than ever before; the quality of performance is higher due to professionalisation; stadiums have better facilities funded by commercial revenue. questions.question: Describe three types of sponsorship in sport, giving a specific example of each.

points.text: Financial sponsorship: Direct monetary payment, e.g. Emirates Airlines sponsoring Arsenal's stadium and shirt for £200m. Equipment sponsorship: Providing kit and sport-specific equipment, e.g. Adidas supplying the kit for the British Olympic team. Facility sponsorship: Naming rights and venue funding, e.g. Etihad Airways sponsoring Manchester City's Etihad Stadium.
